description:
**File**: `src/fetcher/feed_fetcher_concurrent.cr:128-150`

**Severity**: P1 (resource leak under load)

When the outer `select` times out and closes `result_channel`, the
inner fiber continues running the full `Fetcher.pull` (up to
`FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) and only discovers the closed channel when
it tries to send. The fiber stays alive (tracked by FiberTracker),
holds `feed`, `config`, and may itself spawn more fibers for redirects.

With 207+ feeds refreshing every 30 min and a few slow hosts, this
can keep 10-20 inner fibers alive indefinitely, each holding their
captured `feed`/`config`/result structures.

**Fix sketch**:
1. Wrap the inner fetch in a cancellation-aware `Future`-style abstraction
2. The outer fiber sets a `done` flag (or closes a sentinel channel)
   on timeout; the inner fiber checks it before/after blocking calls
3. Or: use `Crystal::Fiber.timeout` (if available) on the inner fetch

**Alternative**: Move to a poll-and-bail design where the inner fiber
checks `result_channel.closed?` after every long-running call.

**Related**: `quickhea-vnk` EPIC description lists this in its
"feed_fetcher_concurrent.cr" leak vector, but no child ticket
specifically tracks the inner-fiber leak.

Found during code review 2026-06-18, see
`planning/code-review-2026-06-18.md` §1.2.
title: FeedFetcherConcurrent inner fetch fiber leaks when outer times out
